solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's extremely rotten to mob rock musician

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it about, so the letters around it are jumbled
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rock musician thinks it is rotten to be mobbed by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely rotten' gives RN; with ITS and TOMOB that pool is shuffled, 'rock' signalling the anagram while posing as a music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the brass slide instrument is one kind of musician.

clue.text: Could be box number husband lost

indicators.note: lost says a letter goes missing from the word before it

parts.note: three is a number

explanation.surface: Someone at a PO box finds a husband has lost the number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' marks box as an example, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree, so box is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Liberal Democrat in centre of Alloa upset the police

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the whole assembly is read upwards, backwards
in places the political pieces inside the middle letters of Alloa
the centre of a word here is all its letters but the first and last

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem in central Alloa has upset the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of Alloa is LLO; LIBD goes inside to make LLIBDLO, which 'upset' turns over. Alloa is a small Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Bill is British slang for the police force collectively.

clue.text: But I bet he somehow reversed order to face the situation

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way
reversed says the word for order is read backwards

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them

explanation.surface: Someone bets that he reversed an order in order to face up to things.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTIBETHE rearranged ('somehow') gives BITETHEBU; TELL read backwards ('reversed') gives LLET.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept and confront an unpleasant situation is an idiom meaning grit your teeth and endure it.

clue.text: Stripped underwear for a pound

indicators.note: stripped means the word's outer covering, its first and last letters, is removed

parts.note: knickers are women's underpants

explanation.surface: Someone strips off underwear for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: A nicker is British slang for one pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for one pound sterling, the British currency unit.

clue.text: Sees term out — this one?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone sees out an academic term, wondering whether it is this one.
explanation.walkthrough: SEESTERM rearranged by 'out'; the whole clue also describes the answer, a term that a student sees out.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-year teaching period at a college or university is a kind of academic term.

clue.text: Writer's love for one book

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis is a British novelist
I is the Roman numeral one
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A writer's love stands in for a single book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love for one' means O replaces I in AMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic book of the Old Testament carries this name.

clue.text: Man's address is around New York's cathedral?

indicators.note: is around says the form of address encloses the next piece

parts.note: Mister is the form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A man's address is near New York's cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' is a false unit: New gives N; York belongs to the definition, as York Minster is the city's famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: York's great church is York Minster, so a large church of this sort is what the question mark hints at.

clue.text: Do rats enter Canterbury? That's poor

indicators.note: enter says the pieces go inside the diocese word

parts.note: Canterbury is an archbishop's see, a diocese
to do someone is to swindle or con them
rats and drat are both mild exclamations of annoyance

explanation.surface: Do rats get into Canterbury? That would be shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior in quality, below the best, so poor is a synonym.

clue.text: Recalled quote that's long, having amazing memory

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite
to long for something is to be dying for it, so long means die

explanation.surface: A long quotation recalled by someone with a remarkable memory.
explanation.walkthrough: CITEDIE read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes vivid, near-photographic recall of images, an amazing kind of memory.

clue.text: Stupid male's given gold coin that's forged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: forged means made or faked, so the letters of the word coin are reworked

explanation.surface: A stupid man is given a forged gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish in the manner of an idiot, so a synonym for stupid.

clue.text: One who makes you beam and beam

definitions.meaning: a cheerful person who brings happiness and smiles
a shaft of light from the sun

explanation.surface: Someone who makes you smile, and a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a sunbeam; figuratively a cheerful person who brightens others' day.

clue.text: Thus unprepared shopper visits supermarket without enthusiasm?

definitions.meaning: a shopper without a shopping list goes about it in this way, read literally

explanation.surface: A shopper with no plan trudges listlessly round the supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as list-less-ly: lacking a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargically, with no energy or interest, the usual sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Brown belt

definitions.meaning: to belt someone is to thrash or beat them

explanation.definitionFit: A light brown shade, and slang for beating, as in tan someone's hide.

clue.text: Choice between one party and another's supporter for workplace?

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, a British political party
or is the word that offers a choice between two things
a Tory is a supporter of the Conservatives, another party

explanation.surface: A voter's choice between one party and a rival party's supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read as Lab or a Tory: Labour and the Conservatives (Tories) are Britain's main parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A room where scientists conduct experiments is a scientist's place of work; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Venomous type catches general napping

indicators.note: catches means the snake holds the general inside it

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A venomous snake catches a general while he is napping.
explanation.definitionFit: Napping means dozing or sleeping, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Look more attractive, said Jack

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: see is look, and fairer means more attractive

explanation.surface: Jack remarked that someone looked more attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or jack tar, is an old name for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack is a traditional nickname for a sailor, who travels by sea.

clue.text: English mother's family mostly raised to be successful without help

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: one's flesh and blood is one's family, so flesh means family

explanation.surface: An English mother's family is raised to succeed unaided.
explanation.walkthrough: E, DAM and FLES make EDAMFLES, which 'raised' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rose by their own efforts, without inheritance or patronage.

clue.text: Former pupil's successfully treated? That's made unclear

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil; OB's is OBS
a patient successfully treated is cured

explanation.surface: A former pupil has been cured, but how is not clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscured means hidden or blurred, so made unclear is a synonym.

clue.text: Bird is close, eating worm up

indicators.note: eating means the sealing word swallows the other piece

parts.note: to seal is to close

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the worm is read backwards

parts.note: a lug is a lugworm

explanation.surface: A bird close by, eating a worm.
explanation.walkthrough: LUG turned 'up' is GUL, eaten by SEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A common coastal bird of the gull family.

clue.text: Gates surely holds back Apple

indicators.note: back means those letters are read in reverse
holds says the letters are contained within the words

explanation.surface: Bill Gates surely keeps back Apple, his rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'Gates surely' contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A russet is a variety of eating apple with rough brownish skin.

clue.text: Left wearing torn blouse? That can be explained

indicators.note: wearing means the garment has the letter inside it
torn means ripped apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leaving in a torn blouse? There's an explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOUSE torn becomes SOUBLE, with L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A soluble problem is solvable or explicable.

clue.text: Join Academy headed by German composer

indicators.note: headed by in a down clue means placed on top, before the rest

parts.note: to link is to join

explanation.surface: Joining an academy run by a German composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a nineteenth-century Russian composer.

clue.text: Eliminating every second Afghan military leader

indicators.note: removing each second letter leaves the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Killing every other Afghan military leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is an Ottoman commander or chief officer.

clue.text: Jockey feels silly in an apathetic way

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A jockey feels silly riding without spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Without vigour or animation, the manner of an apathetic person.

clue.text: Court order, one producing gags? That's about right

indicators.note: about says the joker surrounds the letter

parts.note: a wit is a person who makes jokes

explanation.surface: A court order to gag someone? About right.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written command from a court.

clue.text: One cracking old joke cheers prickly sort

parts.note: a pun is a play on words, a joke

indicators.note: cracking means getting into, so the numeral breaks into the thanks word

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
I is one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone cracks an old joke and says cheers to a prickly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly pear cactus genus, so a spiny plant is a prickly sort.

clue.text: Two Scotsmen turn round large beauty salon

indicators.note: round says the names go around the size letter
turn means the two names are read backwards

parts.note: Rab is a typical Scottish man's name
Ian is another typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: Two Scotsmen turn round a large beauty parlour.
explanation.walkthrough: RABIAN turned gives NAIBAR, which goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon specialising in manicures is a type of beauty salon.

clue.text: Ring wife to avoid hue and cry

indicators.note: to avoid says these letters are kept out of the colour word

parts.note: yellow is a hue
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: Ring your wife to avoid a hue and cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hue and cry' is a phrase but splits: hue is wordplay, cry the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout loudly, a synonym for cry.

clue.text: Crack troops come in handy for obliteration

indicators.note: come in says the pieces go inside the skilful word

parts.note: handy means skilful, deft
crack as an adjective means first-rate, ace
troops are men

explanation.surface: Crack troops prove handy in an act of destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Defacing spoils or effaces a surface, a kind of obliteration.
